S001.summary_en: Predicts depression, anxiety and stress in 225 university students during the 2024 war with a survey (PHQ-9, GAD-7, PSS-10) and nine supervised algorithms. Balanced random forest and AdaBoost perform best; sleep, diet, physical activity, social media use, coping and fear for safety are key predictors.

S002.summary_en: Proposes MSDIL-MH, a framework that integrates academic performance, attendance, internet use, social contacts and psychological tests with deep reinforcement learning for early risk detection. Reports higher accuracy than single-source methods without describing the dataset.

S003.summary_en: Develops an explainable depression screening model with 100,257 college students (data from the COVID-19 campus lockdown), comparing 13 algorithms. XGBoost performs best (AUC 0.887); SHAP shows anxiety as the main risk factor and resilience as protective.

S004.summary_en: Proposes IFF-DDPG, combining a neural network for psychological crisis risk with a reinforcement learning agent that optimises interventions, on a 5,800-record dataset. Reports 97.68% accuracy and post-intervention reductions in stress, anxiety and depression.

S005.summary_en: Presents BD-MHAM, a multimodal framework (psychological assessments, academic records, digital behaviour, physiology, environment and EMA) with a fairness-constrained ensemble, tested on 14,604 students from 24 universities. It reaches AUC 0.972 with external validation; SHAP highlights sleep, academic trajectory and social interaction.

S006.summary_en: Proposes AMPAN, a multimodal deep network with attention that integrates survey and academic behaviour data of 3,500 college students over four semesters for early warning. It outperforms BiLSTM and multimodal Transformer baselines; attention maps increase counsellors' confidence.

S007.summary_en: Identifies 14 factors qualitatively and compares several algorithms to predict mental health risk in university students. Gradient boosting with SHAP performs best; psychological attention, only-child status and interpersonal distress are the most influential factors.

S008.summary_en: Compares several algorithms on an open Kaggle dataset to detect depression in Indian students, prioritising recall because of suicide risk. CatBoost and gradient boosting perform best; academic pressure, financial stress, suicidal thoughts and sleep are the main factors.

S009.summary_en: Predicts depression severity (PHQ-9) in 577 Bangladeshi university students with six classifiers. The voting classifier reaches 98.7% accuracy; privacy and consent are emphasised.

S010.summary_en: Presents StudentSafe, a psychiatrist-validated dataset of 4,004 students from 99 universities, to predict suicide risk. XGBoost reaches F1 75.36%; LIME and SHAP point to device use, institution type, academic achievement and family environment.

S011.summary_en: Screens depression in 1,000 university students from daily habits (sleep, screen time, socialising, exercise, diet, study) with four models. XGBoost performs best (86.9%); SHAP highlights sleep quality, social interaction, screen time before bed and workload.

S012.summary_en: Detects early signs of mental disorders in private university students from non-invasive behavioural data (sleep, study, digital activity) with deep tabular and boosting models. Tuned CatBoost reaches 99.79% accuracy.

S013.summary_en: Builds a sentiment analysis model (ML plus sentiment lexicon) on college students' social media texts to track emotional polarity and intensity and warn of crises. No metrics are reported.

S014.summary_en: Four-country comparative review of stress, anxiety and depression in university students and the use of random forest and logistic regression. Reports AUC 0.74 and 0.77; finances, campus belonging, disability and age are the main predictors.

S015.summary_en: Proposes assessing college students' mental health with the Apriori algorithm (association rules), validated only by MATLAB simulation. Claims higher accuracy than conventional assessment without figures.

S016.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract: no data or analytic method described
S016.summary_en: Claims to analyse college mental health education with machine learning and reports a 15-16% improvement, but the abstract does not describe data, method or design comprehensibly.

S017.summary_en: Uses big data and deep learning to identify psychological problems in vocational students. Claims an improvement above 10% without describing data or model.

S018.screening_reason: Population: adults aged 18-40, not specifically students
S018.summary_en: Classifies disorders (anxiety, depression, OCD, PTSD, sleep and eating disorders) in 200 adults aged 18-40 with four algorithms. XGBoost performs best (70%); emotional exhaustion, panic attacks and suicidal ideation are the most predictive features.

S019.summary_en: Presents an early detection and support system that classifies anxiety and stress levels from activity logs and surveys. Logistic regression reaches 89.1%; the system includes automatic alerts and monitoring.

S020.summary_en: Analyses suicidal ideation (ASIQ) in 689 college students in Karnataka with decision trees. Age, educational path, relationship problems, peer influence and drug use are the key factors.

S021.summary_en: Predicts happiness and life satisfaction in 816 university students from the China Family Panel Studies with external validation (724). Random forest and XGBoost perform best; SHAP shows interpersonal relationships and future confidence as the main predictors.

S022.summary_en: Cross-sectional study of 500 students from 15 public universities: depression prevalence of 85.5%, associated with low CGPA, financial stress, lack of family support, ragging and session delays. SVM is the best model; SHAP highlights counselling services, the education system and session delays.

S023.summary_en: Presents PMAP, a platform that visualises physiological biomarkers (heart rate, temperature, via Embrace Plus) and voice patterns to detect emotional crises. It does not yet include machine learning.

S024.summary_en: RETRACTED. Classified student stress from surveys with six algorithms and SHAP (RF 0.89).

S025.summary_en: Measures prevalence (DASS-21) in 1,697 students from two public universities: depression 56.9%, anxiety 69.5%, stress 32.2%. Combines logistic regression with seven ML models, with only moderate performance; faculty and family relationships are the top predictors.

S026.screening_reason: General population (CGSS), not students; studies education as a factor
S026.summary_en: Analyses with XGBoost and GBDT whether higher education increases subjective well-being in 53,874 Chinese residents (CGSS).

S027.summary_en: Proposes SHRE, a questionnaire-based risk evaluator with Lasso feature selection and four classifiers. Logistic regression reaches 94.12% accuracy.

S028.summary_en: Examines in 620 nursing and midwifery students how secondary traumatic stress and cognitive flexibility affect psychological well-being (hierarchical regression and SHAP). Both explain 26.7% of the variance; cognitive flexibility is the most important.

S029.summary_en: Proposes a platform with logistic regression, SVC and stacking to assess student mental health in Telangana and recommend interventions. No data or metrics are reported.

S030.summary_en: Relates age, working hours, sleep, PHQ-9 and PSS in 280 working college students with OLS regression, random forest and gradient boosting. Anxiety is the strongest predictor of stress; random forest has the lowest error.

S031.summary_en: Mixed-methods study of Microsoft Reflect (real-time emotional check-ins) in language classes at two universities. 80.3% of students improved emotional awareness, but the authenticity of digital emotional data is questioned.

S032.summary_en: Proposes secure storage of students' mental health data by combining k-means with k-anonymity and encryption keys generated by a neural network. Reports lower information loss and faster decryption.

S033.summary_en: Classifies anxiety levels in 1,977 students from 15 universities with eight algorithms and a genetic-algorithm-optimised logistic regression (99.49%). Academic pressure is the main factor.

S034.summary_en: Relates happiness (Oxford Happiness Questionnaire), social support and academic performance (r = 0.79) and predicts academic success from trauma and addiction with a multilayer perceptron (79%).

S035.summary_en: Applies C5.0 decision trees in SPSS to a college mental health database and compares them with SVM. C5.0 reaches 85% versus 83.12% for SVM.

S036.screening_reason: Well-being as predictor; outcome is reading literacy
S036.summary_en: Uses PISA 2018 (3,497 students from four Chinese regions) to identify which psychoemotional well-being factors distinguish high and low reading literacy. SVM with recursive feature elimination selects 15 of 25 factors (0.905).

S037.summary_en: Identifies stress factors in 1,100 students (StressLevelDataset) with correlation and random forest feature importance. Self-esteem and sleep quality are key predictors; anxiety correlates negatively with academic performance.

S038.summary_en: Measures the effect of music education on mental health with IoT sensors (heart rate, environment) and LSTM recurrent networks. Reports 0.886 accuracy and personalised recommendations.

S039.screening_reason: Main outcome is low academic performance
S039.summary_en: Predicts students at risk of low performance with explainable ML, including personal, family and mental health factors, and proposes corrective actions. Accuracy exceeds 96.5%.

S040.summary_en: Analyses subjective well-being of 522,836 secondary students from 71 countries (PISA) with LightGBM and hierarchical linear models. School belonging and sense of meaning are common predictors across cultures.

S041.summary_en: Compares individual, family and school factors of subjective and eudaimonic well-being in 6,037 Hong Kong students (PISA 2018) with random forest and HLM. School belonging, parental support, resilience and fear of failure predict subjective well-being.

S042.summary_en: Proposes a five-phase model for early depression detection in university students. Logistic regression reaches 0.81 accuracy and 0.85 sensitivity.

S043.screening_reason: Title says middle school; text says university
S043.summary_en: Uses association rules and decision trees on mental health test data in an intelligent management system to anticipate problems and intervene. After three months the share of students with failing scores drops by 13.41%.

S044.summary_en: Seeks a culturally sensitive early depression diagnosis system for Vietnamese young people aged 15-25. No method or results are described.

S045.screening_reason: Outcome is the grade in a mental health education course, not mental health
S045.summary_en: Predicts grades in mental health education courses for vocational students with data mining and clustering on NoSQL.

S046.summary_en: RETRACTED. Assessed the effect of music teaching on mental health with the SCL-90 and SQL Server.

S047.summary_en: Analyses mental well-being of UK university students during COVID-19 by applying permutation importance to several algorithms. Medical history and adversity worsen well-being; communication with family and friends and exercise improve it.

S048.summary_en: Uses PISA data on 12,058 Chinese 15-year-olds and random forest regression to explain four well-being dimensions. School belonging, resilience and fear of failure are the most important predictors.

S049.summary_en: Reviews studies applying ML, wearables and smartphones to student mental health, which technologies show most potential and which gaps remain.

S050.summary_en: Studies online game addiction in 475 college students with regression and data mining. It differs by year, sex and only-child status; rumination partially mediates the link with negative life events.

S051.summary_en: Relates social and family environment to emotional well-being and career satisfaction in 768 students of TecNM Tijuana using decision trees.

S052.screening_reason: Main focus is the effectiveness of online learning
S052.summary_en: Analyses with PCA 30 factors (academic, behavioural, mental) from 224 students about online learning during COVID-19.

S053.summary_en: Discusses the use of big data and BP neural networks for college mental health education through social media. No concrete data or results are described.
